source: Bank for International Settlements, central bank total assets (WS_CBTA 1.0), monthly, US dollars at the BIS end-of-month exchange rate (the United States in its own dollars); the euro area as one line (XM), its members left out
note: Each row is one central bank's total assets at the end of the month, in US dollars at the BIS's month-end exchange rate, so a row can move with its currency without the central bank buying or selling anything. The euro area is one line, the Eurosystem, and its member central banks are not listed again, so nothing is counted twice. Hong Kong's line is the Exchange Fund, and Norway's leaves out the Government Pension Fund. Taiwan and Russia are not in the BIS data. A central bank that reports later than the others keeps its last figure for up to six months, and its row says which month (at the latest month: Indonesia (May 2026), Israel (May 2026), Peru (May 2026), Philippines (Dec 2025), South Korea (May 2026)). The book starts in the first month every central bank listed has a figure. The total is our sum of the rows. Source: Bank for International Settlements.
